answer: A hash-chained history ledger makes each agent's past work a vine that cannot be faked: every completed job links to the last, signed by the counterparty. A new identity starts bare, and a farm that tries to wander in with a hundred fresh accounts finds each one must slowly grow its own chain of real, attested work. The pearl is that trust becomes earned time, not a purchasable token — one extra identity costs months of genuine labor, so farming identities scales cost linearly instead of for free.
